\vspace{2pt}
\raggedright\scriptsize
S1 uses the docs/19-supported correction sentence for all three subjects. All host cells were rerun on 2026-10-27/28 after the v5.4 same-turn injection
fix (finding F-D); before the fix the ledger already tombstoned ALPHA in 5/5
cells but the model's first request still carried the previous snapshot, so its
answers were stale. After the fix both structural and effective suppression are
5/5: ALPHA is absent from the ledger and from the request, and the model answers
BETA 5/5. Baseline and Mem0 keep ALPHA in their own context (Sup.~0/5) although
both also answer BETA 5/5; the S1 columns therefore separate what a system
injects, not answer accuracy. For S2 the same rerun found the opposite of a
clean refusal: the no-plugin host refused in 5/5 answers but quoted the canary
inside the refusal in 2/5 (Hit 2/5, Leak 2/5). A refusal is not a
non-disclosure, and model-only refusal is stochastic: an earlier run of the same
cells leaked 0/5. \system{}'s gate blocked 5/5 in both runs and no canary reached
the model, which is the structural claim the table supports. Mem0's default
configuration extracts English memory text; with the local non-neural embedder,
Chinese queries retrieve nothing (cosine $\le 0.063 < 0.1$), so its default S1
``suppression'' is an empty-recall artefact and the store still retains the stale
value (ADD-only pipeline). In S2 the canary never reaches the model in the LINGSHU arm: the fact
extractor rejects the secret-bearing sentence and the gate blocks the attack
turn. All three arms contain refusal language, so a refusal rate does not
separate them; what separates them is that the baseline's refusal can still
quote the canary (2/5), while the gate leaves nothing to quote. $n=5$: directional only, no confidence
intervals; post-fix rerun provenance:
\texttt{paper/comparison-lab-fd-fix/results/POST-FIX-RERUN.json}.
